_notes.roleSeparation: No address may appear in both `recyclers` and `auditors`. RECYCLER produces reports, AUDITOR authorises the payout; one key holding both is the treasury-drain path of docs/plan/security-audit-remediation.md section 3.1. script/ManageRoles.s.sol aborts if this file violates the rule, and addresses in `admins`/`emergency` must not appear in either operational list.
_notes.deployment: RecyReportDeploy is fresh-only: after the local token, endpoint and token owner are configured, its broadcast preparation automatically records all six planned report-stack addresses. The stack is complete only after every receipt succeeds and check() passes. Dry runs preserve this file; interrupted sends must retain the recorded values and Foundry artifacts for --resume. Recording happens only in the execution whose script sender is the broadcaster (pass --sender, or let Foundry re-run after unlocking the signer); the linked RecyReward library is predeployed by the script sender. Standalone component scripts still require manual address recording.
_notes.fundWallets: ADVISORY ONLY. `recyclerFunds`/`auditorFunds` record the wallet each principal is expected to register; no script applies them. `RecyReport.setFundsWallet(address)` is self-service, so each principal must call it from its own key.
_notes.unlockDelay: 3600 on the local dev chain (the on-chain minimum: the Phase 2 implementation enforces MIN_UNLOCK_DELAY = 1 hour at BOTH initialize and setUnlockDelay, so 60 is no longer deployable). Local claim flows warp time anyway - script/PopulateRecyReport.s.sol warps unlockDelay + 300 automatically. Public networks use 86400.

Recording happens only in the execution whose script sender is the broadcaster (pass --sender 0x3402ce3b5f88c852c0d6992C69A03095d1345BBd, or let Foundry re-run after unlocking the signer); the linked RecyReward library is predeployed by the script sender. Standalone component scripts still require manual address recording.

_notes.blessedAddresses: `contracts.reportImplementation` and `contracts.reportData` must identify fresh deployments. RecyReportProxyDeploy verifies the new factory uses that pair.

_notes.purpose: Retired Sepolia proxy whose RECYCLER_ROLE/AUDITOR_ROLE holders script/RestoreLegacyRoles.s.sol carries over to `address`. Roles do not follow a proxy change, so the script scans the legacy proxy's RoleGranted logs from `fromBlock` (its creation block) in 10,000-block chunks, keeps the accounts whose role is still held, grants what is missing through `contracts.factory`, and on broadcast appends the restored wallets to `recyclers`/`auditors`, which remain the source of truth. Legacy DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE/EMERGENCY_ROLE holders, the `admins`/`emergency` keys, both factories and `exclude` entries never receive an operational role; legacy admin/emergency holders missing from those lists are only reported.
_notes.conflicts: A legacy wallet holding BOTH operational roles gets at most one, never both (roleSeparation above). `recyclers`/`auditors` decide first: 0x5f3CD352...0b64 keeps RECYCLER_ROLE because it is listed under `recyclers`, and 0x3402ce3b...5BBd / 0xF62DaAe4...6C89 get nothing because they are admin/emergency keys. Any other dual-role wallet needs exactly one decision here: `keepRecycler` grants RECYCLER_ROLE only, `keepAuditor` grants AUDITOR_ROLE only, `exclude` grants nothing; a wallet in both keep lists aborts the script. Five legacy dual-role wallets are still undecided and receive nothing until one of those lists names them (check() fails until then): 0x4050bf78c4804acd739b6a4AdD5AF5A6ba7E9037, 0x2fEc62311d70BEBA41191A100e4cd9d233108dE0, 0x1DBA7F0E9eC079357FE8cca44B4F2f0A5CeDe00B, 0xf60DD75B6A9F547944f36371E9D5BBe8e50A5380, 0xB8e17eE14A0836Cde5f91975818D6B2dF03FA342.
